title: Conduct Search Engine Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
reference_info: Identify what sensitive design and configuration information of the application, system, or organization is exposed directly (on the organization's site) or indirectly (via third-party services). Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/01-Conduct_Search_Engine_Reconnaissance_for_Information_Leakage

title: Fingerprint Web Server
reference_info: Determine the version and type of a running web server to enable further discovery of any known vulnerabilities. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/02-Fingerprint_Web_Server

title: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
reference_info: Identify hidden or obfuscated paths and functionality through the analysis of metadata files. Extract and map other information that could lead to a better understanding of the systems at hand. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/03-Review_Webserver_Metafiles_for_Information_Leakage

title: Attack Surface Identification
reference_info: Enumerate all web applications within scope. Identify DNS names, domains, and virtual hosts associated with the target. Discover additional domains and subdomains using passive and active DNS techniques. Analyze digital certificates and Certificate Transparency logs for additional hostnames. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/04-Attack_Surface_Identification

title: Review Web Page Content for Information Leakage
reference_info: Review web page comments, metadata, and redirect bodies to find any information leakage. Gather JavaScript files and review the JS code to better understand the application and to find any information leakage. Identify if source map files or other frontend debug files exist. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/05-Review_Web_Page_Content_for_Information_Leakage

title: Identify Application Entry Points
reference_info: Identify possible entry and injection points through request and response analysis. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/06-Identify_Application_Entry_Points

title: Map Execution Paths Through Application
reference_info: Map the target application and understand the principal workflows. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/07-Map_Execution_Paths_Through_Application

title: Fingerprint Web Application Framework
reference_info: Fingerprint the components used by the web applications. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/08-Fingerprint_Web_Application_Framework

title: Fingerprint Web Application
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/09-Fingerprint_Web_Application

title: Map Application Architecture
reference_info: Understand the architecture of the application and the technologies in use. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/10-Map_Application_Architecture

title: Test Network Infrastructure Configuration
reference_info: Review the applications' configurations set across the network and validate that they are not vulnerable. Validate that used frameworks and systems are secure and not susceptible to known vulnerabilities due to unmaintained software or default settings and credentials. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/01-Test_Network_Infrastructure_Configuration

title: Test Application Platform Configuration
reference_info: Ensure that default and known files have been removed. Validate that no debugging code or extensions are left in the production environments. Review the logging mechanisms set in place for the application. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/02-Test_Application_Platform_Configuration

title: Test File Extensions Handling for Sensitive Information
reference_info: Enumerate sensitive file extensions that might contain raw data such as scripts or credentials Validate that no system framework bypasses exist for the rules that have been set Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/03-Test_File_Extensions_Handling_for_Sensitive_Information

title: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
reference_info: Find and analyse unreferenced files that might contain sensitive information. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/04-Review_Old_Backup_and_Unreferenced_Files_for_Sensitive_Information

title: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
reference_info: Identify hidden administrator interfaces and functionality. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/05-Enumerate_Infrastructure_and_Application_Admin_Interfaces

title: Test HTTP Methods
reference_info: Enumerate supported HTTP methods. Test for access control bypass. Test HTTP method overriding techniques. title: Test HTTP Strict Transport Security
reference_info: Review the HSTS header and its validity. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/07-Test_HTTP_Strict_Transport_Security

title: Test File Permission
reference_info: Review and identify any rogue file permissions. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/09-Test_File_Permission

title: Test for Subdomain Takeover
reference_info: Enumerate all possible domains (previous and current). Identify any forgotten or misconfigured domains. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/10-Test_for_Subdomain_Takeover

title: Test Cloud Storage
reference_info: Assess that the access control configuration for the storage services is properly in place. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/11-Test_Cloud_Storage

title: Test for Content Security Policy
reference_info: Review the Content-Security-Policy header or meta element to identify misconfigurations. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/12-Test_for_Content_Security_Policy

title: Test Path Confusion
reference_info: Make sure application paths are configured correctly. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/13-Test_for_Path_Confusion

title: Test Other HTTP Security Header Misconfigurations
reference_info: Identify improperly configured security headers. Assess the impact of misconfigured security headers. Validate the correct implementation of required security headers. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/02-Configuration_and_Deployment_Management_Testing/14-Test_Other_HTTP_Security_Header_Misconfigurations

title: Test Role Definitions
reference_info: Identify and document roles used by the application. Attempt to switch, change, or access another role. Review the granularity of the roles and the needs behind the permissions given. title: Test User Registration Process
reference_info: Verify that the identity requirements for user registration are aligned with business and security requirements. Validate the registration process. title: Test Account Provisioning Process
reference_info: Verify which accounts may provision other accounts and of what type. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/03-Identity_Management_Testing/03-Test_Account_Provisioning_Process

title: Testing for Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
reference_info: Review processes that pertain to user identification (*e.g.* registration, login, etc.). Enumerate users where possible through response analysis. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/03-Identity_Management_Testing/04-Testing_for_Account_Enumeration_and_Guessable_User_Account

title: Testing for Weak or Unenforced Username Policy
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/03-Identity_Management_Testing/05-Testing_for_Weak_or_Unenforced_Username_Policy

title: Testing for Credentials Transported over an Encrypted Channel
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/01-Testing_for_Credentials_Transported_over_an_Encrypted_Channel

title: Testing for Default Credentials
reference_info: Determine whether the application has any user accounts with default passwords. Review whether new user accounts are created with weak or predictable passwords. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/02-Testing_for_Default_Credentials

title: Testing for Weak Lock Out Mechanism
reference_info: Evaluate the account lockout mechanism's ability to mitigate brute force password guessing. Evaluate the unlock mechanism's resistance to unauthorized account unlocking. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/03-Testing_for_Weak_Lock_Out_Mechanism

title: Testing for Bypassing Authentication Schema
reference_info: Ensure that authentication is applied across all services that require it. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/04-Testing_for_Bypassing_Authentication_Schema

title: Testing for Vulnerable Remember Password
reference_info: Validate that the generated session is managed securely and do not put the user's credentials in danger. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/05-Testing_for_Vulnerable_Remember_Password

title: Testing for Browser Cache Weaknesses
reference_info: Review if the application stores sensitive information on the client-side. Review if access can occur without authorization. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/06-Testing_for_Browser_Cache_Weaknesses

title: Testing for Weak Authentication Methods
reference_info: Determine the resistance of the application against brute force password guessing using available password dictionaries by evaluating the length, complexity, reuse, and aging requirements of passwords. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/07-Testing_for_Weak_Authentication_Methods

title: Testing for Weak Security Question Answer
reference_info: Determine the complexity and how straight-forward the questions are. Assess possible user answers and brute force capabilities. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/08-Testing_for_Weak_Security_Question_Answer

title: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
reference_info: Determine whether the password change and reset functionality allows accounts to be compromised. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/09-Testing_for_Weak_Password_Change_or_Reset_Functionalities

title: Testing for Weaker Authentication in Alternative Channel
reference_info: Identify alternative authentication channels. Assess the security measures used and if any bypasses exists on the alternative channels. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/10-Testing_for_Weaker_Authentication_in_Alternative_Channel

title: Testing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
reference_info: Identify the type of MFA used by the application. Determine whether the MFA implementation is robust and secure. Attempt to bypass the MFA. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/04-Authentication_Testing/11-Testing_Multi-Factor_Authentication

title: Testing Directory Traversal File Include
reference_info: Identify injection points that pertain to path traversal. Assess bypassing techniques and identify the extent of path traversal. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization_Testing/01-Testing_Directory_Traversal_File_Include

title: Testing for Bypassing Authorization Schema
reference_info: Assess if unauthenticated, horizontal, or vertical access is possible. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization_Testing/02-Testing_for_Bypassing_Authorization_Schema

title: Testing for Privilege Escalation
reference_info: Identify injection points related to privilege manipulation. Fuzz or otherwise attempt to bypass security measures. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization_Testing/03-Testing_for_Privilege_Escalation

title: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References
reference_info: Identify points where object references may occur. Assess the access control measures and if they're vulnerable to IDOR. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization_Testing/04-Testing_for_Insecure_Direct_Object_References

title: Testing for OAuth Weaknesses
reference_info: Determine if OAuth2 implementation is vulnerable or using a deprecated or custom implementation. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization_Testing/05-Testing_for_OAuth_Weaknesses

title: Testing for Session Management Schema
reference_info: Gather session tokens, for the same user and for different users where possible. Analyze and ensure that enough randomness exists to stop session forging attacks. Modify cookies that are not signed and contain information that can be manipulated. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/01-Testing_for_Session_Management_Schema

title: Testing for Cookies Attributes
reference_info: Ensure that the proper security configuration is set for cookies. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/02-Testing_for_Cookies_Attributes

title: Testing for Session Fixation
reference_info: Analyze the authentication mechanism and its flow. Force cookies and assess the impact. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/03-Testing_for_Session_Fixation

title: Testing for Exposed Session Variables
reference_info: Ensure that proper encryption is implemented. Review the caching configuration. Assess the channel and methods' security. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/04-Testing_for_Exposed_Session_Variables

title: Testing for Cross Site Request Forgery
reference_info: Determine whether it is possible to initiate requests on a user's behalf that are not initiated by the user. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/05-Testing_for_Cross_Site_Request_Forgery

title: Testing for Logout Functionality
reference_info: Assess the logout UI. Analyze the session timeout and if the session is properly killed after logout. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/06-Testing_for_Logout_Functionality

title: Testing Session Timeout
reference_info: Validate that a hard session timeout exists. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/07-Testing_Session_Timeout

title: Testing for Session Puzzling
reference_info: Identify all session variables. Break the logical flow of session generation. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/08-Testing_for_Session_Puzzling

title: Testing for Session Hijacking
reference_info: Identify vulnerable session cookies. Hijack vulnerable cookies and assess the risk level. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/09-Testing_for_Session_Hijacking

title: Testing JSON Web Tokens
reference_info: Determine whether the JWTs expose sensitive information. Determine whether the JWTs can be tampered with or modified. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/10-Testing_JSON_Web_Tokens

title: Testing for Concurrent Sessions
reference_info: Evaluate the application's session management by assessing the handling of multiple active sessions for a single user account. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/11-Testing_for_Concurrent_Sessions

title: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting
reference_info: Identify variables that are reflected in responses. Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any). title: Testing for Stored Cross Site Scripting
reference_info: Identify stored input that is reflected on the client-side. Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any). Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/02-Testing_for_Stored_Cross_Site_Scripting

title: Testing for HTTP Verb Tampering
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/03-Testing_for_HTTP_Verb_Tampering

reference_info: Identify the back end and the parsing method used. Assess injection points and try bypassing input filters using HPP. reference_info: Identify SQL injection points. Assess the severity of the injection and the level of access that can be achieved through it. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/05-Testing_for_SQL_Injection

title: Testing for LDAP Injection
reference_info: Identify LDAP injection points. Assess the severity of the injection. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/06-Testing_for_LDAP_Injection

title: Testing for XML Injection
reference_info: Identify XML injection points. Assess the types of exploits that can be attained and their severities. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/07-Testing_for_XML_Injection

title: Testing for SSI Injection
reference_info: Identify SSI injection points. Assess the severity of the injection. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/08-Testing_for_SSI_Injection

title: Testing for XPath Injection
reference_info: Identify XPATH injection points. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/09-Testing_for_XPath_Injection

title: Testing for IMAP SMTP Injection
reference_info: Identify IMAP/SMTP injection points. Understand the data flow and deployment structure of the system. Assess the injection impacts. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/10-Testing_for_IMAP_SMTP_Injection

title: Testing for Code Injection
reference_info: Identify injection points where you can inject code into the application. Assess the injection severity. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/11-Testing_for_Code_Injection

title: Testing for Command Injection
reference_info: Identify and assess command injection points. Bypass special characters and OS commands filter. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/12-Testing_for_Command_Injection

title: Testing for Format String Injection
reference_info: Assess whether injecting format string conversion specifiers into user-controlled fields causes undesired behavior from the application. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/13-Testing_for_Format_String_Injection

title: Testing for Incubated Vulnerability
reference_info: Identify injections that are stored and require a recall step to the stored injection. Understand how a recall step could occur. Set listeners or activate the recall step if possible. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/14-Testing_for_Incubated_Vulnerability

title: Testing for HTTP Response Splitting
reference_info: Identify user-controlled input that is reflected into HTTP response headers. Assess whether CR (`\r`) and LF (`\n`) characters can be injected into response headers. Determine the potential impact of successful HTTP Response Splitting attacks, such as cache poisoning or client-side exploitation. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/15-Testing_for_HTTP_Response_Splitting

title: Testing for HTTP Request Smuggling
reference_info: Identify request boundary inconsistencies between frontend and backend components Detect classic CL/TE desynchronization vulnerabilities Evaluate protocol translation logic (HTTP/2 → HTTP/1.1) Assess H2C upgrade handling and downgrade safety Confirm backend request queue poisoning Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/16-Testing_for_HTTP_Request_Smuggling

title: Testing for Host Header Injection
reference_info: Assess if the Host header is being parsed dynamically in the application. Bypass security controls that rely on the header. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/17-Testing_for_Host_Header_Injection

title: Testing for Server-side Template Injection
reference_info: Detect template injection vulnerability points. Identify the templating engine. Build the exploit. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/18-Testing_for_Server-side_Template_Injection

title: Testing for Server-Side Request Forgery
reference_info: Identify SSRF injection points. Test if the injection points are exploitable. Asses the severity of the vulnerability. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/19-Testing_for_Server-Side_Request_Forgery

title: Testing for Mass Assignment
reference_info: Identify requests that modify objects Assess if it is possible to modify fields never intended to be modified from outside Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/20-Testing_for_Mass_Assignment

title: Testing for CSV Injection
reference_info: Identify CSV/spreadsheet export features that include untrusted input. Verify whether attacker-controlled values are interpreted as formulas when the export is opened in common spreadsheet applications. Check whether separator/quote injection can move a dangerous prefix to the start of a cell. Validate whether mitigations remain effective in Microsoft Excel after saving and re-opening the CSV. Assess practical impact based on who opens the export and how it is used. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/21-Testing_for_CSV_Injection

title: Testing for Prototype Pollution
reference_info: Identify functions and libraries that recursively merge, clone, or assign user-controlled properties. Determine whether user input can reach and modify `Object.prototype`. Identify gadgets that turn prototype pollution into a concrete impact. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/22-Testing_for_Prototype_Pollution

title: Testing for Insecure Deserialization
reference_info: Identify entry points where the application accepts serialized objects from untrusted urces (for example, HTTP headers, parameters, or cookies). Determine the serialization format used by the application. Assess whether serialized input is validated or restricted prior to deserialization. Evaluate whether manipulation of serialized data leads to unsafe behavior or security pact. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Input_Validation_Testing/23-Testing_for_Insecure_Deserialization

title: Testing for Improper Error Handling
reference_info: Identify existing error output. Analyze the different output returned. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/08-Testing_for_Error_Handling/01-Testing_For_Improper_Error_Handling

title: Testing for Stack Traces
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/08-Testing_for_Error_Handling/02-Testing_for_Stack_Traces

title: Testing for Weak Transport Layer Security
reference_info: Validate the service configuration. Review the digital certificate's cryptographic strength and validity. Ensure that the TLS security is not bypassable and is properly implemented across the application. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/09-Testing_for_Weak_Cryptography/01-Testing_for_Weak_Transport_Layer_Security

title: Testing for Padding Oracle
reference_info: Identify encrypted messages that rely on padding. Attempt to break the padding of the encrypted messages and analyze the returned error messages for further analysis. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/09-Testing_for_Weak_Cryptography/02-Testing_for_Padding_Oracle

title: Testing for Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
reference_info: Identify sensitive information transmitted through the various channels. Assess the privacy and security of the channels used. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/09-Testing_for_Weak_Cryptography/03-Testing_for_Sensitive_Information_Sent_via_Unencrypted_Channels

title: Testing for Weak Cryptographic Primitives
reference_info: Provide a guideline for the identification weak encryption or hashing uses and implementations. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/09-Testing_for_Weak_Cryptography/04-Testing_for_Weak_Cryptographic_Primitives

title: Test Business Logic Data Validation
reference_info: Identify data injection points. Validate that all checks are occurring on the backend and can't be bypassed. Attempt to break the format of the expected data and analyze how the application is handling it. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/01-Test_Business_Logic_Data_Validation

title: Test Ability to Forge Requests
reference_info: Review the project documentation looking for guessable, predictable, or hidden functionality of fields. Insert logically valid data in order to bypass normal business logic workflow. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/02-Test_Ability_to_Forge_Requests

title: Test Integrity Checks
reference_info: Review the project documentation for components of the system that move, store, or handle data. Determine what type of data is logically acceptable by the component and what types the system should guard against. Determine who should be allowed to modify or read that data in each component. Attempt to insert, update, or delete data values used by each component that should not be allowed per the business logic workflow. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/03-Test_Integrity_Checks

title: Test for Process Timing
reference_info: Review the project documentation for system functionality that may be impacted by time. Develop and execute misuse cases. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/04-Test_for_Process_Timing

title: Test Number of Times a Function Can Be Used Limits
reference_info: Identify functions that must set limits to the times they can be called. Assess if there is a logical limit set on the functions and if it is properly validated. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/05-Test_Number_of_Times_a_Function_Can_Be_Used_Limits

title: Testing for the Circumvention of Work Flows
reference_info: Review the project documentation for methods to skip or go through steps in the application process in a different order from the intended business logic flow. Develop a misuse case and try to circumvent every logic flow identified. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/06-Testing_for_the_Circumvention_of_Work_Flows

title: Test Defenses Against Application Misuse
reference_info: Generate notes from all tests conducted against the system. Review which tests had a different functionality based on aggressive input. Understand the defenses in place and verify if they are enough to protect the system against bypassing techniques. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/07-Test_Defenses_Against_Application_Misuse

title: Test Upload of Unexpected File Types
reference_info: Review the project documentation for file types that are rejected by the system. Verify that the unwelcomed file types are rejected and handled safely. Verify that file batch uploads are secure and do not allow any bypass against the set security measures. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/08-Test_Upload_of_Unexpected_File_Types

title: Test Upload of Malicious Files
reference_info: Identify the file upload functionality. Review the project documentation to identify what file types are considered acceptable, and what types would be considered dangerous or malicious. If documentation is not available then consider what would be appropriate based on the purpose of the application. Determine how the uploaded files are processed. Obtain or create a set of malicious files for testing. Try to upload the malicious files to the application and determine whether it is accepted and processed. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/09-Test_Upload_of_Malicious_Files

title: Test Payment Functionality
reference_info: Determine whether the business logic for the e-commerce functionality is robust. Understand how the payment functionality works. Determine whether the payment functionality is secure. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/10-Business_Logic_Testing/10-Test-Payment-Functionality

title: Testing for DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting
reference_info: Identify DOM sinks. Build payloads that pertain to every sink type. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/01-Testing_for_DOM-based_Cross_Site_Scripting

title: Testing for JavaScript Execution
reference_info: Identify sinks and possible JavaScript injection points. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/02-Testing_for_JavaScript_Execution

title: Testing for HTML Injection
reference_info: Identify HTML injection points and assess the severity of the injected content. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/03-Testing_for_HTML_Injection

title: Testing for Client-side URL Redirect
reference_info: Identify injection points that handle URLs or paths. Assess the locations that the system could redirect to. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/04-Testing_for_Client-side_URL_Redirect

title: Testing for CSS Injection
reference_info: Identify CSS injection points. Assess the impact of the injection. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/05-Testing_for_CSS_Injection

title: Testing for Client-side Resource Manipulation
reference_info: Identify sinks with weak input validation. Assess the impact of the resource manipulation. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/06-Testing_for_Client-side_Resource_Manipulation

title: Testing Cross Origin Resource Sharing
reference_info: Identify endpoints that implement CORS. Ensure that the CORS configuration is secure or harmless. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/07-Testing_Cross_Origin_Resource_Sharing

title: Testing for Clickjacking
reference_info: Assess application vulnerability to clickjacking attacks. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/09-Testing_for_Clickjacking

title: Testing WebSockets
reference_info: Identify the usage of WebSockets. Assess its implementation by using the same tests on normal HTTP channels. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/10-Testing_WebSockets

title: Testing Web Messaging
reference_info: Assess the security of the message's origin. Validate that it's using safe methods and validating its input. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/11-Testing_Web_Messaging

title: Testing Browser Storage
reference_info: Determine whether the site is storing sensitive data in client-side storage. The code handling of the storage objects should be examined for possibilities of injection attacks, such as utilizing unvalidated input or vulnerable libraries. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/12-Testing_Browser_Storage

title: Testing for Cross Site Script Inclusion
reference_info: Locate sensitive data across the system. Assess the leakage of sensitive data through various techniques. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/13-Testing_for_Cross_Site_Script_Inclusion

title: Testing for Reverse Tabnabbing
reference_info: Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/14-Testing_for_Reverse_Tabnabbing

title: Testing for Client-side Template Injection
reference_info: Identify the client-side framework and its version used by the application. Detect injection points where user input is reflected into the DOM and processed by the template engine. Assess if the injection allows for arbitrary JavaScript execution (XSS) via the template syntax. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/11-Client-side_Testing/15-Testing_for_Client-Side_Template_Injection

title: API Reconnaissance
reference_info: Find all API endpoints supported by the backend server code, documented or undocumented. Find all parameters for each endpoint supported by the backend server, documented or undocumented. Discover interesting data related to APIs in HTML and JavaScript sent to clients. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/12-API_Testing/01-API_Reconnaissance

title: API Broken Object Level Authorization
reference_info: The objective of this test is to identify whether the API enforces proper **object-level authorization** checks, ensuring that users can only access and manipulate objects they are authorized to interact with. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/12-API_Testing/02-API_Broken_Object_Level_Authorization

title: Testing for Excessive Data Exposure
reference_info: Identify API responses that contain more data than what the client application displays or requires. Detect sensitive fields returned in API responses such as password hashes, authentication tokens, internal object IDs, PII, or infrastructure details. Determine whether the API relies on client-side filtering rather than server-side field selection to control data exposure. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/12-API_Testing/03-Testing_for_Excessive_Data_Exposure

title: API Broken Function Level Authorization
reference_info: The goal of this test is to determine if the API enforces **role or privilege-based access control** to restrict users from accessing or executing functions they are not authorized to use. This ensures that function-level security boundaries are properly enforced. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/12-API_Testing/04-API_Broken_Function_Level_Authorization

title: Testing GraphQL
reference_info: Assess that a secure and production-ready configuration is deployed. Validate all input fields against generic attacks. Ensure that proper access controls are applied. Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/12-API_Testing/99-Testing_GraphQL
